house-rep-lookup.name: House.gov representative lookup and switchboard
house-rep-lookup.outcome: Matches a ZIP code to a House district and your representative in Congress; switchboard (202) 224-3121 connects to any office
house-rep-lookup.limits: ZIP codes can span districts and boundaries were redrawn, so results can be off without a full address; no central email list.
house-rep-lookup.locator: "call (202) 224-3121 for the U.S. House switchboard operator"; "their representative in Congress"

usagov-officials.name: USAGov elected officials directory
usagov-officials.outcome: One page linking to contacts for the president, senators, representatives, governors, state legislators, mayors and county officials
usagov-officials.limits: A directory of links to other sites, not one combined list for an address.
usagov-officials.locator: Local section: mayor search by name, city or population size

cmf-staff-survey.name: Congressional Management Foundation surveys of congressional staff
cmf-staff-survey.outcome: 94% of staff said in-person constituent visits would have some or a lot of influence on an undecided lawmaker; 92% said the same of individualized emails
cmf-staff-survey.limits: Staff perceptions, not measured effects on votes; the 2017 report itself sits behind a registration form and was read through a summary.
cmf-staff-survey.locator: "in-person visits from constituents" would have "some" or "a lot" of influence

resistbot.name: Resistbot text-message service
resistbot.outcome: Text resist to 50409 and have one message delivered to your senators, representative, governor, state legislators and mayor
resistbot.limits: Free delivery is by email; postal mail and fax are a paid member feature. A form-style message carries less weight than a personal one.
resistbot.locator: "Text resist to 50409 or use our web bot."

dol-comment-guide.name: Labor Department guide to commenting on proposed rules
dol-comment-guide.outcome: The Wage and Hour Division reviews every comment submitted by the deadline; comments go through regulations.gov and are posted publicly
dol-comment-guide.limits: One agency's page; comments inform the rule but are not votes.
dol-comment-guide.locator: "reviews and considers every comment submitted before the deadline"

wa-committee-signin.name: Washington State Legislature committee sign-in
wa-committee-signin.outcome: Anyone can search a bill and sign in online to a committee hearing with a position and comments, or sign up to testify
wa-committee-signin.limits: One state's system; other states differ.
wa-committee-signin.locator: Sign-in information includes "your registration, positions, and comments"

open-states.name: Open States legislative data
open-states.outcome: Free data on state legislators and bills; a lookup returns the legislators for a given location
open-states.limits: Needs a free key and coordinates, not a street address; local government coverage is limited.

portland-state-turnout.name: Portland State University 'Who Votes for Mayor' pilot
portland-state-turnout.place: Portland, Charlotte, Detroit and St. Paul
portland-state-turnout.outcome: Mayoral turnout as low as 7% (Charlotte primary); registered voters 65+ about 10 times as likely to vote as those 18-34
portland-state-turnout.limits: Four cities, mayoral races only; percentages are of registered voters.
portland-state-turnout.locator: Lowest turnout 7% in Charlotte's primary; age gap roughly "10 times"

nyc-pb.name: New York City Council participatory budgeting
nyc-pb.outcome: In the 2016-2017 cycle, 102,800 residents voted on how to spend over $40 million in capital funds across 31 council districts
nyc-pb.limits: Only participating districts; capital projects only; later cycles had smaller budgets.
nyc-pb.locator: "the 2016-2017 Participatory Budgeting cycle"; "102,800 New Yorkers voted"

chicago-49th-pb.name: Chicago 49th Ward participatory budgeting
chicago-49th-pb.outcome: Alderman Joe Moore let residents decide about $1 million of ward capital money; over 1,300 voted, funding beach showers, heated bus shelters and a dog park; about 400 people attended nine neighborhood meetings the previous fall, per the May 2012 article
chicago-49th-pb.limits: One ward; skeptics say small organized groups can push through pet projects.
chicago-49th-pb.locator: Over 1,300 ballots on 21 projects; about 400 attended "the nine neighborhood meetings last fall"

ireland-assembly.name: Irish Citizens' Assembly
ireland-assembly.outcome: 99 randomly chosen members; 64% backed changing the abortion amendment; the 2018 referendum passed with 66.4%
ireland-assembly.limits: Recommendations were advisory; the outcome on abortion itself remains deeply contested.
ireland-assembly.locator: "broadly representative of society in terms of gender, age, social class and regional spread"

ostbelgien-council.name: Ostbelgien permanent Citizens' Council
ostbelgien-council.outcome: A 24-person council drawn by lot sets topics for citizens' panels; parliament must debate their recommendations twice within a year
ostbelgien-council.limits: Recommendations are not binding; one small region.
ostbelgien-council.locator: "obliged to have two debates on the recommendations within one year"

france-climate-convention.name: French Citizens' Convention for Climate
france-climate-convention.outcome: 149 recommendations; 3 rejected outright, 46 fully included in the climate bill, others partly included or weakened
france-climate-convention.limits: Source is an advocacy group's write-up; other counts of what became law differ.
france-climate-convention.locator: "46 proposals are included in the Bill"

vtaiwan-uber.name: vTaiwan consultation on ride-hailing
vtaiwan-uber.outcome: About 3,000 people used Pol.is over four weeks; consensus points shaped talks, and the government agreed in 2016 to ratify them
vtaiwan-uber.limits: Government is not required to follow vTaiwan; tensions over Uber continued afterward.
vtaiwan-uber.locator: May 23, 2016: government agreed to ratify the consensus points

alaska-rcv-repeal.name: Alaska Ballot Measure 2 repeal vote
alaska-rcv-repeal.outcome: Repeal of open primaries and ranked-choice voting failed by 664 votes out of 340,110; sponsor plans another try in 2026
alaska-rcv-repeal.limits: Unofficial count at the time of the article; voters split almost evenly.
alaska-rcv-repeal.locator: Final margin of 664 out of 340,110 votes

rcv-state-bans.name: State bans on ranked-choice voting
rcv-state-bans.place: Ten states including Florida, Tennessee, Idaho and Kentucky
rcv-state-bans.outcome: Ten states banned ranked-choice voting between 2022 and 2024
rcv-state-bans.limits: Reported by a pro-reform outlet that does not give ban supporters' reasons.
rcv-state-bans.locator: 2024 bans: Alabama, Kentucky, Louisiana, Mississippi and Oklahoma

town-hall-project.name: Town Hall Project event list
town-hall-project.outcome: Volunteers research every district for public events with members of Congress and publish a searchable list with email alerts
town-hall-project.limits: Founders describe progressive values; the list says it is for everyone. On 2026-10-19 townhallproject.com showed an unrelated gambling site, so the project appears inactive.
town-hall-project.locator: "We research every district and state for public events with members of Congress"

legistorm-town-halls.name: LegiStorm count of August recess town halls
legistorm-town-halls.outcome: Members of Congress held more than 900 town hall-style events in one August recess; 94% were in person
legistorm-town-halls.limits: One recess in 2013; no trend data, and numbers vary by party and year.
legistorm-town-halls.locator: More than 900 town hall-style events during the August recess
